Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the final phase of play on Day 2, with roughly 45 minutes left on the clock. The primary objective for Zimbabwe's opening pair, Ben Curran and Brian Bennett, will be to negotiate this tricky period without any damage. Sam Cook will start with the new ball for England. Here we go!
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Zimbabwe have it all to do to save this Test. Brian Bennett was the standout performer by a country mile, showing composure and intent in an otherwise underwhelming batting display. While Craig Ervine and Sean Williams offered glimpses of resistance, the touring side desperately needed more from their experienced duo to mount a meaningful reply. Heading into the second innings, the visitors will require a massive collective effort not only from the senior players but also from the rest of the batting unit. Back in a bit for Zimbabwe's second innings.

Zimbabwe have been folded for 265 in their first innings. With a lead of 300 runs, England have decided to enforce the follow-on. A decision very much on expected lines, especially with this being a four-day Test and rain forecast on Day 3. The hosts will now look to pile the pressure and push for an innings win. Shoaib Bashir was superb with his guile and deception and finished with three wickets, while on the pace bowling front, Ben Stokes looked the most threatening and had a couple of scalps to his name,

For Zimbabwe, Brian Bennett continued his aggressive batting in this session too, as he notched up the fastest hundred for Zimbabwe in Tests in 97 balls and dare I say he is still out there playing his shots without fear. However, with half the side back it’s going to be a herculean task for the visitors. England will look to wrap this up as quickly as possible. Do join us in a bit for the post-tea session.

SESSION SUMMARY - 27 overs, 137 runs and 4 wickets. An eventful session comes to an end. A lot of action in that session. There were runs as well as wickets in there. England are clearly in the driver’s seat. They got four wickets in the session as their captain, Ben Stokes, led from the front getting two wickets towards the fag end of the session and ensuring they are well ahead in the game. Shoaib Bashir did bowl well on a wicket which isn’t offering much and he was rightly rewarded as he picked the wickets of two left-handers.

... DAY 2, SESSION 2 ...

With 73 runs on the board at the loss of one wicket, Zimbabwe have surely got off to a good start. There have been some nervy moments here and there with the new ball for the Zimbabwean batters, but the surface has largely remained unresponsive. Once the shine of the ball goes away, the tourists have a real chance to put on a good total here. So, do join us in a bit for the post-lunch session of this 4-Day Test.

Zimbabwe, too, would have felt better as they managed to take 3 wickets, which was equal to what they managed to pick in the whole of yesterday. Then the visitors came out to bat and their openers showed intent from the word go, especially Brian Bennett, who smashed three boundaries in the first over of their innings. Ben Curran fell to a beautiful delivery from Gus Atkinson and post that, Craig Ervine has come to the crease and he has looked fairly comfortable for his brief stay.

SESSION SUMMARY - 24.3 overs, 140 runs and 4 wickets. Lunch on Day 2 here in Trent Bridge. One would call it a shared session between the two sides. England batters started the session with the intent to score as many as possible and they fairly succeeded at that as they scored 67 runs in 8.3 overs before declaring the innings. Harry Brook had a major role, as he scored the bulk of the runs in that phase of play.
